helpful: Provisioned application.txt gave the State's full argument and the procedural history.
CourtListener RECAP had the Sixth Circuit's published stay order and dissent within hours, which was the single most useful input.
Corpus rows carry application_kind, capital_case, referred_to_court, response_requested and amicus_briefs, which made a quick applicant-class cut possible.
gaps: fedcourts query has no filter for applicant class (State vs prisoner) or ask (vacate vs stay), so isolating State vacatur applications meant pulling 200-row sweeps and filtering client-side; the withdrawn sweep cost ~200 MB of ranged reads.
The response and reply were on the SCOTUS docket at snapshot but not provisioned as documents; on a response-filed cell the response text is the moment's defining input.
The statpack interim section has no cut by applicant class or by ask, so the pooled 10.5% rate is a poor anchor for a State's application to vacate an execution stay.
notes: Query rows print caption/date fields under case_name / date_filed / date_decided rather than caption / filed_at; a one-line key listing in docs/cli.md would save a wasted call.
